messages:
anya: idea from today's arch sync: make precision decisions prompt-aware by tagging layers with confidence thresholds and letting the preprocessor supply lightweight hints.

tomas: can you sketch the difference vs global-profile fallback?

anya: global profile = one quality floor for whole model. new approach = per-layer confidence vector + prompt hints so runtime only relaxes layers unlikely to harm output. saves cost but keeps critical parts high fidelity.

reza: how do we get per-layer confidence cheaply? we can't run full shadows every request.

anya: offline: calibrate sensitivity per-model/quant via a small eval sweep to produce sensitivity_map. online: use cheap proxies (last-token surprisal, prefix-token-entropy, kv-cache logit changes) to mark current request's sensitive regions.

kai: operational concerns: per-layer heterogeneity increases kernel permutations and complicates batching. batching could explode if every request chooses different layer bits.

tomas: limit choices: runtime exposes at-most-3 layer classes per model (high/med/low). grouping maps real layer indices to classes so kernel set is bounded. if batch heterogeneity > threshold, fall back to uniform model-level precision.

anya: example profile manifest: ```json
{
  "name":"layer-aware-econ-1",
  "allowed_classes":["high","med","low"],
  "class_bitwidths":{"high":8,"med":8,"low":4},
  "sensitivity_map_compressed":"base64..",
  "preproc_policy":"auto-oracle"
}
```

reza: preproc_policy auto-oracle? pls clarify.

anya: two modes: auto (SDK extracts hints heuristically), oracle (customer-provided hints in request). default=auto. hints are optional. runtime must ignore untrusted hints from public requests unless customer asserts auth.

kai: caching: if some layers use lower bits and others not, our KV serialization must encode precision class per-layer and invalidate on profile change. Also we need to mark entries with the profile hash.

ops-bot: note: add profile-hash to cache keys and invalidate when profile artifact changes.

reza: monitoring: need aggregated "layer-degradation_score" and heatmaps in console. Also sample-based headwise diffs for a small shadow fraction.

anya: rollout playbook: 1) create profile staged=true, 2) shadow sample 1% (per-profile shadow runner), 3) collect layer deltas and user-facing metric deltas for 72h, 4) promote to live if < thresholds.

kai: safety: global kill-switch + per-profile hard-fallback to model-level precision. Also hysteresis: don't switch live classes more than once per X tokens per endpoint.

aniya: (typo fix) anya: also: add a preflight simulator in console so admins can estimate cost delta and regression risk before flipping.

reza: implement proto: I'll make a small library that computes online sensitivity proxies and emits per-request candidate classes.

tomas: I'll add kernel-grouping logic and a fallback path when batching can't honor heterogeneity.

ops-bot: perf task queued: per-layer-batching-sim on redwood-7b-qpt, ETA 24h.

anya: thanks all. I'll write a compact RFC follow-up with schema, rollout steps, and a sample eval bundle.
